prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: pixel-art gargoyle animation draft atlas for an artist; not a presentation board.
Reference image: the attached small orange-armored mechanical stone gargoyle, preserve its identity exactly: tan skull and claws, two cyan crystal horns, cyan ribcage reactor, charcoal joints, orange segmented folded bat wings with round mechanical hinges.
Create a square transparent PNG sprite atlas, exactly 1000 x 1000 pixels, precisely 5 columns by 5 rows of equal 200 x 200 pixel cells. No grid lines, labels, text, shadows, ground, decorative background or other creatures. EACH ROW is a distinct FIVE-FRAME animation, chronological LEFT TO RIGHT. Camera fixed, right-facing three-quarter view, same character scale and anatomy throughout. Crisp true pixel-art, hard pixel clusters, limited palette, no antialiasing, no smooth gradients. EVERY character fully fits within its own cell with margins, even extended attacks, absolutely no overlapping neighboring cells. Each character silhouette occupies at least 128 pixels in width and 128 pixels in height but stays under 184 x 164 pixels. Common ground/foot baseline 164 pixels from the top of each cell. No scaling between frames. No projectile, laser or nova effects beyond small attached core/throat glow; effects are separate. Keep armor proportions identical to reference. Wings stay grounded; no flight. Animation poses must actually change across five frames, readable anticipation, action and follow-through.
Rows TOP TO BOTTOM:
1. idle: five distinct subtle breathing poses: neutral, chest rise, horn/core pulse, wing hinge settle, return close to neutral.
2. walk: five grounded walking poses, alternating claw-foot plants with weight shifting; no translation across cell.
3. claw-sweep: five attack poses: front claw draws back, crouched anticipation, forward horizontal sweep, full reach, follow-through.
4. claw-backhand: five attack poses: opposite claw crosses chest, torso coils, wide horizontal backhand, extended arc, recoil.
5. claw-heavy: five attack poses: claw rises, overhead heavy anticipation, downward slam, ground-contact compressed pose, recovery.
